_comment: Deterministic chemistry -> bioactivity-axis lookup. Converts 'the model knows nikkomycin/HSAF are antifungal' into a table any runner applies. Matched against (modeb_class + note + KCB anchor), lowercased; axes are checked in the order listed (most specific bioactivity first). Extend the keyword lists rather than relying on a model to recognise a chemistry. KCB anchors are similarity, not identity; axis is a class-level functional hypothesis.

axes_in_priority_order.rationale: polyenes, chitin-synthase-inhibitor nucleosides (nikkomycin/polyoxin), and polycyclic tetramate macrolactams (HSAF family) are antifungal even though their class names do not contain 'antifungal'

compound_rules.when: product class includes 'nucleoside' OR CCTT trigger T43-NUC_nucleoside
compound_rules.and_context: strain/region carries a chitin-axis marker (CGAD CBM_CHITIN or GlcNAc, or a chitin-synthase/chitinase domain)
compound_rules.label: chitin-synthase-inhibitor nucleoside (nikkomycin / polyoxin class) — candidate, verify by HRMS + Candida chitin-synthase panel
compound_rules.rationale: the antifungal nucleosides in actinomycetes are the chitin-synthase inhibitors; the KCB anchor is often only a genome match named 'nucleoside' with no compound name, so name-matching fails — gate on the chitin context instead.
compound_rules.without_context_axis: nucleoside-antibiotic candidate (axis uncertain) — do not default to antibacterial

_audit_note: Keywords must match strings antiSMASH/KCB actually emit (genome-match descriptions, MIBiG product fields), NOT textbook chemistry names. Audit new keywords against real anchors before trusting them.

priority_policy._never_drop_meaning: A BGC mapping to any of these axes is ALWAYS delivered in every lead output. If it falls below the top-lead cutoff it is emitted in a 'Low-priority / adjacent' partition, never omitted. No ranking cutoff silently removes a chemistry-relevant lead (this is the BGC008 fix: AF_auto 23.7 dropped it from a top-AF-first list).

priority_floor._meaning: Nucleoside-class BGCs (product 'nucleoside' OR CCTT T43-NUC) are rare and high-value — chitin-synthase-inhibitor antifungals (nikkomycin/polyoxin) and polar antibiotics. Floor their lead priority to HIGH regardless of AF_auto/AB_auto score. The floor governs RANKING only; the bioactivity AXIS is still set by the gated chitin rule (high priority does not assert antifungal, it asserts 'screen this').

priority_policy.af_auto_scorer_rule: After Lead_tier_auto is assigned: (1) if product is nucleoside/T43-NUC -> Lead_tier_auto = max(current,'High'); (2) when emitting any antifungal or antibacterial track, do NOT truncate at a score cutoff — partition into 'Primary' (above cutoff) and 'Low-priority / adjacent' (below), so every chemistry-relevant lead is shown.
